known_issues: Canonical task/work state is data/tasks.json; work_queue files and routes are compatibility aliases until cleanup finishes.
Legacy /work-queue and /api/work-queue names still exist for compatibility and may confuse new users.
Numeric work priority maps onto canonical task priority labels, so old work CLI priority display can look different after conversion.
Local AI features depend on Ollama being reachable and the configured models being installed.
Onboarding recommends commands but does not yet provide one-click clipboard helpers for copying them.
Onboarding can guide service startup, but starting dashboard/API still happens through existing desktop/dashboard controls.
Real tray support requires optional pystray and Pillow dependencies; watcher mode remains the dependency-free fallback.
Desktop shell currently provides launcher/status/chat controls, not full tray integration.
Desktop companion requires Tkinter to be available in the local Python install.
Browser live polling depends on the dashboard-integrated local API being reachable.
Live refresh updates counts and status text, but full table rows still require a page reload.
Dashboard forms currently support creation, not full edit/delete CRUD for every item.
API is intentionally local-only by default and has no authentication layer for public exposure.
Chat-to-action currently uses deterministic intent matching rather than full local-AI intent parsing

Test recommendations are rule-based and not yet deeply AI-analyzed

AI review quality depends on the local Ollama model installed
Long patch/run/report ids are annoying to copy manually

No memory compaction/summarization workflow yet
Goals were previously loose strings in self_model.json and project metadata
Task execution is supervised and whitelist-only; it does not grant unrestricted terminal access

Guided work sessions still advance only one step at a time and do not provide full autopilot
Approval inbox is explicit and supervised; it does not grant automatic permission to apply or rollback patches.
Settings changes do not bypass safety gates; file edits and rollbacks still require approval workflows.
Watch mode is advisory and does not apply patches, rollback files, approve actions, or run unsafe commands automatically.
Watch loops are bounded and stop when attention is needed instead of running forever.
Dashboard chat console still depends on local Ollama for conversational responses when enabled.

notes: v4.3 added --desktop-tray-status and settings for enabling/disabling tray behavior, startup tray launch, close-to-tray, watcher fallback, and tooltip status updates.
v4.3 added desktop_tray.py with optional pystray/Pillow system tray support, tray status checks, minimize-to-tray behavior, and safe tray menu actions.
Approved file editing added in v0.9. Saved patches can be applied only through an explicit command.
Patch application creates backups under data/backups and logs actions to data/action_log.json.
Rollback support is the next safety layer before command execution.
Rollback system added in v1.0. Applied patches can be restored from backups with explicit command.
Rollback checks current file hash before restoring to avoid overwriting newer work.
Approved command execution added in v1.1. Commands are parsed with shell=False and checked against a whitelist.
Command runner blocks destructive commands, package installs, network calls, shell wrappers, pipes, redirection, and risky git commands.
Test-runner workflow added in v1.2. It runs approved commands through command_runner.py and saves reports under data/test_reports.
Test workflow reports include command results, patch context, and a keep/review-or-rollback recommendation.
Auto-review after patch added in v1.3. It reviews saved test reports and recommends keep, rollback, fix workflow, or manual review.
Test reviews are saved under data/test_reviews and do not execute commands or modify files.
v1.4 adds supervised self-improvement workflow for review, patch, apply, test, and auto-review.
v1.5 added latest/latest-proposed/latest-applied/latest-rolled-back aliases and --latest-ids.
v1.7 adds memory compaction/summarization with archives, dry-run support, summary aliases, and semantic memory rebuild after compaction.
v1.9 adds session planner. It creates read-only next-session plans from goals, maintenance scans, memory summaries, patch state, and test reports.
Session plans are advisory only and do not run commands or apply changes.
